title: Committed Serve Charter: proportional credits, autoscale interlock, and fleet control language
creator: Avery Chen
description: Purpose: Draft a concise, legally-friendly termsheet and operational playbook for committed throughput (tokens/min or requests/s) on Dedicated capacity. This ticket consolidates SLA definition, error budget math, proportional credit algorithm, and the autoscale/failover interlock that prevents unplanned recovery actions from voiding credits. Goals: 1) Provide clear measurable SLOs (quantile + window) for committed serve; 2) Define error budget consumption and crediting formula tied to customer-visible throughput and failover events; 3) Specify autoscale interlock conditions and step-down governance to avoid oscillation; 4) Produce contract-ready prose and a short operational runbook for on-call and customer success.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Termsheet language (<= 2 pages) reviewed by legal and uploaded to Confluence; 2) Error budget formula validated with telemetry team and sample calculations for 3 customers; 3) Autoscale interlock sequence diagrams and API hooks documented; 4) Example credit computation script (python/notebook) checked into repo and a dashboard mock showing measurement windows created; 5) Stakeholder sign-off from Legal, Reliability, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success.
comments: 2025-11-19 - Kickoff: scoped deliverables with Reliability and Legal. Decided to measure throughput SLO as 99th percentile of 'served tokens per minute' over a rolling 24-hour window with daily aggregation for credits.

2025-12-02 - Engineering input (ENG-24101): suggested adding a separate SLO for cold-start degradation due to model swaps; proposal to exclude planned maintenance windows from error budget calculation.
2026-01-07 - Legal feedback: prefer 'Service Commitment' language rather than 'Warranty'; requested explicit definitions for 'degradation', 'partial serve', and 'failover' in the termsheet.

2026-01-20 - Product note: proposed proportional credit algorithm: credit = committed_capacity * max(0, 1 - observed_ratio/threshold) integrated with sliding-window weight; initial thresholds: 95% for full credit, 90% partial, <75% escalates remediation. Shared spreadsheet: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/throughput-credit-models

2026-01-28 - Reliability review: autoscale interlock design v1 posted. Key controls: 1) Prevent automatic capacity reclaim for 30 minutes post-failover; 2) Allow customer-initiated emergency burst override; 3) Backoff policy with exponential cooldown to avoid oscillation. Diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folder/autoscale-interlock-v1
2026-02-03 - Draft termsheet uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/committed-serve-termsheet-draft. Requested legal + sales engineering review by 2026-02-10.

2026-02-09 - Sales Eng review: clarified customer notification requirements and the SLA notice windows (24h notice for scheduled maintenance; 2h active incident notification). Suggested adding an optional premium 'hot-standby' lane for white-glove customers.

2026-02-10 - Current status: In Review.
